# Texas Hold'em in 5 minutes

*Everything a new player needs for their first hand: the deal, the four betting rounds and how the winner is decided.*

3 min read · Updated 2026-09-26

Texas Hold'em is the game most home games play. Each player gets **two private cards**, five **shared cards** are dealt face up in the middle, and the best **five-card hand** wins the pot. You can also win without the best hand, if everyone else folds.

## What you need

- 2 to 10 players (6 to 9 is the sweet spot)
- One standard 52-card deck, no jokers
- Chips and a dealer button
- Someone to deal — in most home games the deal rotates with the button

## Before the cards: the button and the blinds

A **dealer button** marks who is ‘dealer’ for the hand. The two players to its left post forced bets called **blinds**: the **small blind** (usually half) and the **big blind**. Blinds make sure there is always something to play for. After every hand the button moves one seat to the left, so everyone pays the blinds equally.

## One hand, step by step

1. **The deal.** Everyone gets two cards face down, one at a time, starting left of the button.
2. **Preflop betting.** The player left of the big blind acts first. Each player can **fold**, **call** the big blind or **raise**.
3. **The flop.** Three cards are dealt face up in the middle. Another round of betting starts with the first active player left of the button.
4. **The turn.** A fourth card, then a betting round.
5. **The river.** A fifth and final card, then the last betting round.
6. **Showdown.** If two or more players are left, they show their cards. Best five-card hand takes the pot.

> **Your hand + the board:** `A♥ K♥` · Board: `Q♥ 7♥ 2♣ J♥ 9♠`
>
> Five hearts across your cards and the board: an ace-high flush.

## Making your best hand

At showdown you make the best five-card hand from any combination of your two cards and the five on the board. You may use **both**, **one** or even **none** of your own cards. If the best hand is the board itself, everyone still in the hand ties and splits the pot.

> **Tip — Suits never break ties:** A flush in spades is not better than a flush in hearts. When hands are the same type, compare the highest cards; if all five match, it’s a split pot.

## Your options when it’s your turn

| Action | When you can | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Check | Nobody has bet this round | Pass without putting chips in |
| Bet | Nobody has bet this round | Put the first chips in |
| Call | Someone has bet | Match the current bet |
| Raise | Someone has bet | Increase the bet |
| Fold | Any time it’s your turn | Give up the hand |

A betting round ends when every player still in the hand has put in the same amount (or is all-in) and everyone has had a chance to act.

## Three beginner mistakes

- **Playing too many hands.** Most two-card hands should be folded before the flop. See the starting hands guide.
- **Forgetting the board is shared.** If the board shows four hearts, anyone with one heart has a flush.
- **Acting out of turn.** Wait until the action reaches you — it changes what others do.
